title: 13th National Economic and Social Development Plan

period.quote: The 13th National Economic and Social Development Plan (2023-2027) is a second-level plan that acts as a key mechanism to translate the National Strategy into implementation and serves as a framework for the formulation of third-level plans so as to enable relevant development partners to function in support of achieving the targets of the National Strategy within the expected timeframe.

risk_framing.summary: The plan is framed as a response to a period of overlapping shocks and structural transitions. It emphasizes recovery from COVID-19, adaptation to rapid technological change, worsening climate change, ageing, geopolitical and trade shifts, and domestic structural weaknesses such as inequality, low productivity, environmental stress, and weak state capability. It treats these not as isolated issues but as interacting pressures requiring resilience, structural transformation, and stronger preparedness systems.
quotes: The 13th Plan was formulated when the world and Thailand were still facing various limitations due to the COVID-19 pandemic, which not only caused illness and death but also adversely affected economic conditions, impacting the livelihoods of all groups of the population.

In addition, the 13th Plan period fall within a time of rapidly-evolving technological development, worsening climate change, an ageing society in Thailand and many countries around the world, as well as geo-political changes.

The synthesis of the development context and the status of multi-dimensional capitals of Thailand during the 13th Plan was completed by collecting and processing data derived from the outcomes of the 12th National Economic and Social Development Plan, many issues of which still need to be implemented continually; together with assessing the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic that brought about dramatic changes to the global development scenario and affected Thailand in many dimensions; and by contemplating on predictions of key global megatrends that can potentially affect Thailand's future development.

The overexploitations of natural resources beyond the ecosystem's capacity, together with limitations in management, lead to the degradation of natural resources and intensifying environmental problems.
Thailand is highly vulnerable to threats from natural disasters and climate change while having limited capability to cope with disasters and their risks.

vocabulary.gloss: A formal tier in Thailand's planning hierarchy below the National Strategy and above third-level action plans.
Operational plans and action plans of agencies that implement second-level plans.
The plan's 13 priority outcome areas stating what Thailand aims to 'be' or 'have' during the plan period.
Thailand's guiding development philosophy emphasizing moderation, reasonableness, resilience/immunity, knowledge and integrity.
Bio-Circular-Green Economy Model; Thailand's framework for combining innovation-led growth with resource efficiency and environmental sustainability.
Original Equipment Manufacturer; production for others' brands with limited domestic value capture.
Owned Brands Manufacturer; firms producing under their own brands.
Owned Design Manufacturer; firms designing and manufacturing products, implying higher capability than OEM.
Total factor productivity; a measure of efficiency/productivity growth beyond labor and capital inputs.
Households with children or youth facing income or non-income deprivation across specified dimensions, used to target chronic poverty transmission.
Thai People Map and Analytics Platform; the government's data platform used to identify poverty and deprivation.
An integrated approach linking human, animal and environmental health in surveillance and response systems.
Home-Temple-School; a local collaboration model including communities, religious institutions, schools and related local actors.
Plan-Do-Check-Act; the management cycle adopted for implementation and monitoring of the plan.
Thailand's policy vision for restructuring toward innovation-driven, higher-value industry and services.
